purpose: Valacyclovir is used to treat infections caused by certain viruses, including herpes simplex (cold sores and genital herpes), shingles (herpes zoster), and chickenpox. It helps reduce the severity and duration of outbreaks and can also help prevent future outbreaks when taken daily. It does not cure these infections but helps control them.
how_it_works: When you swallow valacyclovir, your body quickly converts it into another medicine called acyclovir. Acyclovir works by blocking the virus from copying itself and spreading in your body. Think of it like putting a stop sign in front of the virus so it cannot grow and cause more damage.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, nausea, stomach pain, vomiting, and dizziness. Some people may also notice feeling tired or having diarrhea. These side effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Drink plenty of water while taking this medicine to protect your kidneys. Rarely, it can cause serious side effects like confusion, shaky movements, or signs of kidney problems such as little to no urination — call your doctor right away if these happen. Always tell your doctor about all other medications you take.
typical_dosing: Dosing depends on what you are treating. For a cold sore outbreak, it is often 2 grams twice in one day, 12 hours apart. For genital herpes outbreaks, it is usually 500 mg to 1 gram taken once or twice daily for several days. For daily suppression to prevent outbreaks, a common dose is 500 mg to 1 gram once a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
